title: SharePoint: SharePoint agents in Teams mobile group chats and meetings
summary: The roadmap facts, admin paths and commands are supported, and the briefing correctly limits the SharePoint agent block to Copilot Chat. The low cost rating nevertheless understates the documented pay-as-you-go consumption route that the briefing itself includes; that route is metered, not just administrator time.

claims.claim: Blocking an agent created using SharePoint only affects Copilot Chat, not OneDrive, SharePoint or Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.

claims.claim: The block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Sites** and select **Active sites**. Select the site you want to configure. Open the **Settings** tab, and then turn **Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot** on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the site.
claims.quote:
You can enable Restricted Content Discovery from the SharePoint admin center or by using PowerShell.
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits site discovery in Copilot and removes site AI entry points, including creating agents.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery also removes AI-powered entry points from these SharePoint sites. Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or **Create pages with AI**.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery leaves existing site permissions and direct access unchanged.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses reaches licence assignment.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the **Billing** > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select **Assign licenses**.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The listed controls are existing general SharePoint agent controls, not documentation specifically for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: "481823" SharePoint upgrade agents Teams mobile platforms roles; SharePoint agents Teams mobile default rollout admin enable disable Graph PowerShell. Read all six control references and Manage access to agents in SharePoint; no reference identifies this mobile roadmap item.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The low cost rating describes indirect cost only despite including the documented pay-as-you-go route for SharePoint agent usage.
claims.quote: Page: "cost: low"; "plus the Microsoft Copilot licence or pay-as-you-go billing". Learn: "Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice."
claims.fix: Set cost to "variable". Replace the cost rationale with "Variable. SharePoint agent usage by users without a Microsoft Copilot licence uses pay-as-you-go billing and appears under the Copilot Studio meter on the Azure invoice; no separate Teams mobile rate is published." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/sharepoint-agents-azure-billing. In Cost and licensing, add "For the existing .agent experience, pay-as-you-go charges appear under the Copilot Studio meter on the Azure invoice."

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, third bullet

claims.fix: Replace this bullet with "Confirm which pilot users hold a Microsoft Copilot licence (controls table, row 3)." Do not add a control row.
